inspectedText: Cross and Jackson tested15 spider-eating spartaeine species with two circuitous routes, only one reaching the prey box. After descending from the viewing tower, prey was no longer visible; subjects sometimes passed the wrong entrance to reach the correct one. All15 species selected the correct walkway significantly more often. The authors propose representational cognition. This is an original empirical abstract, not full methods/results inspection. PMC and EuropePMC body requests failed/captcha; Wiley full endpoint redirected to abstract. Do not assert human-like foresight, intelligence equivalence, exact success rates, or a proven neural mechanism.
